title: Construction Manager Salary: Hourly to Annual Guide with Casual Loading and Super
description: Convert your construction manager salary from hourly to annual using our 38-hour week formula. Add 25% casual loading and see super paid on top. Based on Fair Work and ABS data.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives a gross annual figure before tax and super. If you are casual, add 25% casual loading to your base rate first.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of your base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For example, if your base rate is $30 per hour, casual loading brings it to $37.50 per hour. Super is then calculated on the total ordinary earnings, including the loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on a construction manager salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at the current rate of 12%. Ordinary earnings include your base rate plus any casual loading, but exclude overtime. Super is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $60 per hour rate working 38 hours, super adds about $14,227 annually.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Construction Manager Salary

If you are a construction manager or considering a role in the industry, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual salary is essential for comparing job offers, budgeting, and planning your finances. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week, explains casual loading and superannuation, and draws on official data from the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and the Australian Taxation Office.

### The Basic Formula for Hourly to Annual Conversion

The standard formula to estimate your annual gross salary is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, this becomes:

**Hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your construction manager salary is $60 per hour, the annual gross pay would be $60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. The formula also gives you a fortnightly figure: simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For $60 per hour, weekly pay is $2,280, so fortnightly pay is $4,560 before tax and super.

It is important to note that the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, or $1,004.90 per week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. Most construction managers earn well above these minimums, but award rates may apply depending on your classification under the Building and Construction General On-site Award or a similar instrument. Always check your specific award or enterprise agreement for the correct base rate.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

If you work as a casual construction manager, your employer must pay a 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave such as annual leave and sick leave. When using our [timesheet](/), you can enter your base hourly rate and check a box to add the 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool will calculate it for you.

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at the current rate of 12%. Ordinary earnings include your base rate plus any casual loading, but exclude overtime. Super is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For a construction manager earning $60 per hour, 38 hours per week, the annual super contribution would be approximately $14,227 (12% of $118,560), provided your total ordinary earnings do not exceed the cap. This super is paid on top of your salary, so your total remuneration package is higher than your gross pay.

### Industry Averages vs Job Medians

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings in the construction industry averaged $1,985.30 per week in May 2026. This is an industry average, not the median for a construction manager. Individual salaries vary widely based on experience, location, project size, and employer. The average figure includes all full-time construction roles, from labourers to senior managers, so it should not be used as a benchmark for a specific job. For more detailed pay data, refer to our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) guide or the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) reference tables.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your gross annual salary, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200, then 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies, though the reduction thresholds for singles and families are based on 2025–26 figures as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. For a construction manager earning $118,560, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around $27,000–$29,000, leaving a take-home pay of roughly $89,000–$91,000 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more detailed breakdown.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Resources

Our [timesheet](/), which is the home page, allows you to enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading to see your weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures. It also estimates super and tax based on the latest rates. For award-specific information, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data). If you are comparing salary packaging options, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging). For minimum wage details, check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. And for converting other hourly rates, the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool is helpful.

### Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. Always consult a qualified professional for personal financial advice.
